evidence: Analysis of the SAMs chemical composition as well as chemical analysis of Ru films were performed by XPS on a Theta300 system from Thermo Instruments using a monochromatized Al Kα X-ray source (1486.6 eV) and a spot size of 400 µm in angle resolved mode. FTIR on a Nicolet 6700 from Thermo Scientific, in attenuated total reflection (ATR) mode was used to investigate alterations of the SAMs layer and SAM removal by acetic acid. Thickness of the SAMs layer was determined by XRR on a Bede MetrixL system and by SE on a Spectra FX CD system from KLA Tencor. Surface morphology was visualized by SEM imaging using a Hitachi SU8000 SEM tool. The carbon content in the Ru films deposited on Cu surface significantly depends on the deposition temperature and varies from ~ 20 % when the ALD is performed at 225 ºC, to ~ 4 % when ALD is performed at 325 ºC. The carbon content in the Ru layers deposited on Si oxide surface is around 5 ± 1 % and it does not change with the AL/ temperature. The Ru areal concentration on Cu surface ~ 100·1015 at/cm2, which corresponds to Ru thickness of 14 nm assuming Ru density of 12.36 g/cm3. The intensity of the CH2/CH3 organic peaks measured by ATR-FTIR is not decreased after exposing the coated Si oxide samples to the diluted acetic acid cleaning step. The data is consistent with the DETA layer modification occurring at 250 °C, which results in N-C bonds scission in favour of C-C/C=C bonds formation. The mass, thickness and WCA change of the DETA film after ALD Ru were measured. The carbon content in the Ru films deposited on Cu surface significantly depends on the deposition temperature and varies from ~ 20 % when the ALD is performed at 225 ºC, to ~ 4 % when ALD is performed at 325 ºC. The carbon content in the Ru layers deposited on Si oxide surface is around 5 ± 1 % and it does not change with the ALD temperature. The observed Ru ALD inhibition on Cu oxide surface at low temperatures can be exploited for a selective Ru deposition process on Cu oxide with respect to Si oxide in a MoM selectivity scheme. In-situ XPS measurements were performed at the temperature of 250 °C and a pressure of 10-9 mBar. The Si2p XPS peak at 103.2 eV attributed to the Si-O-Si bonds in the SiO2 and DETA layer does not change after annealing. The N1s XPS spectra are shown. The N1s peak component at 399.1 eV is attributed to the DETA primary amino terminal groups (NH2) and secondary amino functional groups (NH). The C1s peak shown in Figure 8c shifts towards lower binding energy, indicating the loss of C-N/ C-O bonds (286 eV) in favour of C-C/C=C bonds formation (284.9 eV) after the thermal treatment. The data is consistent with the DETA layer modification occurring at 250 °C, which results in N-C bonds scission in favour of C-C/C=C bonds formation. The mass, thickness and WCA change of the DETA film after ALD Ru were measured. The maximum number of ALD cycles was limited to 150 to make sure that no ruthenium is present on the DETA surface (based on the RBS results shown in Figure 2b). The mass of the samples decreases after ALD with a variation not correlated to the number of ALD cycles. The average mass decrease is 0.8∙10-4 ± 0.2∙10-4 g, which is ~ 13 % of the pristine DETA-derived film’s mass. According to the SE thickness measurements, shown in Figure 9b, the DETA layer thickness does not change within the measurement error. The WCA of DETA-terminated surface increases after exposure to molecular oxygen at 250 °C, which can be explained by the loss of the hydrophilic amino groups. Additional IR measurements such as FTIR and ATR can be performed to analyze the deamination process. The measurements must be performed in-situ or in inert atmosphere after degas in order to avoid the presence of H2O peaks on IR spectra as they overlap with amino-peaks of the DETA-derived film.
